lines.japanese: 制服に着替えて廊下へ出ると、小鳩の部屋のふすまが小さく開いていた。
lines.english: I changed into my uniform and stepped into the hall. The sliding door to Kobato’s room stood slightly open.

lines.japanese: ちらりと中を窺ったが、すでに布団は上げられていて部屋は無人だった。妹の早起きに感心しながら、僕はそっとふすまを閉める。
lines.english: I glanced inside, but the bedding had already been put away and the room was empty. Impressed that my sister had risen so early, I quietly closed the door.

lines.japanese: そして視線は廊下の突き当たりへ移る──
lines.english: Then my eyes moved to the far end of the hall—

lines.japanese: ──今日も固く閉じている羽田家の洋間。いつもは気にもならなかったけど、なぜだか今日は注意をひかれた。
lines.english: —to the Western-style room in the Haneda house, shut tight as ever. Ordinarily I gave it no thought, but for some reason it caught my attention today.

lines.japanese: 叔父さんからは、大事なものを保管していると聞いている。いったいなんのための部屋なんだろう。
lines.english: My uncle had told me that important things were stored there. What was the room actually for?

lines.japanese: そんなことを考えながら階段を下りた。
lines.english: Still wondering, I went downstairs.

lines.japanese: 洗面所で顔を洗い、仏壇に線香を供えてから居間へ入った。
lines.english: I washed my face, offered incense at the family altar, and entered the living room.

lines.japanese: 先にいた小鳩が、きのうと同じように、骨惜しみもせず朝食を用意してくれた。僕がやたら誉めちぎったせいか、メニューもほとんど同じのパン食だった。
lines.english: Kobato was already there. As she had yesterday, she had spared no effort in preparing breakfast for me. Perhaps because I had praised it so extravagantly, the menu was almost the same: bread again.

lines.japanese: “５：妹と毎日会話をする”
lines.english: “5. Speak with my sister every day.”

lines.japanese: 正直、後悔していた。日課にしたのはやり過ぎだったと思う。
lines.english: Honestly, I regretted it. Making this an everyday thing had been too much.

lines.japanese: 「そういえばネットで見たんだけど、パンケーキのパンって、食べるパンじゃなくてフライパンのパンらしいよ」
lines.english: “Hey, I saw online that the *pan* in *pancake* is the frying-pan kind, not *pan* like our word for bread.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. Really?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、食パンの食っていうのは、もともとフライパンと区別するために付いたって説もあるしね。だからつまり、食べるパンってのを強調する意味で？」
lines.english: “There’s even a theory that the ‘food’ in our word for sliced bread was added to distinguish it from a frying pan. To make clear which *pan* you can eat, I guess?”

lines.japanese: 「はー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「でもいちばん有名なのは、菓子パンに対して主食パンと呼ばれるようになったっていう説みたい」
lines.english: “But apparently the most famous theory is that it came from ‘staple-food bread,’ to tell it apart from sweet buns.”

lines.japanese: 「ほー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 例によって、食卓を飾るのは細くて短い会話だった。
lines.english: As usual, the conversation at our table was thin and short.

lines.japanese: 「そかー、うんー……」
lines.english: “I see. Mm…”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は箸で目玉焼きを切りわけながら、独り言のように小声で呟いている。妹が沈黙を塗りつぶしてくれているあいだに、兄は次の言葉を急ぎ探した。
lines.english: Kobato divided her fried egg with her chopsticks, murmuring softly as though to herself. While my sister painted over the silence, her brother hurried to find his next words.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ねえ。そういえばさ、昨日のニュースどうだった？」
lines.english: “Oh, hey. Come to think of it, what happened with that news story yesterday?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日のニュース？」
lines.english: “Yesterday’s news?”

lines.japanese: 「そうほら、朝やってたじゃない。柳木原で乱闘騒ぎとか何とか」
lines.english: “You know, the one they showed in the morning. Something about a brawl in Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、昨日のニュース」
lines.english: “Oh. Yesterday’s news.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、うん。あの後どうだった？」
lines.english: “Right, that one. What happened after that?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日のニュース……あの後は……」
lines.english: “Yesterday’s news… After that…”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は箸の先をくわえたまま考えて、やがて顔をくいっと斜めに振った。
lines.english: Kobato considered the question with the tips of her chopsticks still in her mouth, then cocked her head sharply to one side.

lines.japanese: 「とくには」
lines.english: “Nothing in particular.”

lines.japanese: 「とくには？」
lines.english: “Nothing?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、スタジオでめがねのひとが難しいこと言って、おわり」
lines.english: “Yeah. A guy with glasses in the studio said a bunch of hard stuff, and that was it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……あー、そうなんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh… I see…”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: おわり。
lines.english: The end.

lines.japanese: 思ったより延びなかった──
lines.english: That had not lasted as long as I hoped—

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: ──あ、いや、まだ延長戦があるみたいだ。
lines.english: —ah. No. Apparently we were going into overtime.

lines.japanese: 「あのニュース、気になるの？」
lines.english: “Are you curious about that story?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、それは一応」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, kind of.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでって……だって、ねえ、近場の事件だし？」
lines.english: “Why…? Well, it happened nearby, didn’t it?”

lines.japanese: そんな風にわざわざ食事の手を止めて尋ねられたって、べつに、ただのミーハーな野次馬根性としか答えようがない。きのうは学校でも気にしてるひと多かったみたいだし。
lines.english: Even though she’d gone so far as to stop eating and ask, all I could say was that I was shallowly chasing a trend and rubbernecking. A lot of people at school seemed curious yesterday too.

lines.japanese: 「まだ犯人も捕まってないんでしょ。あ、犯人って言うのか分かんないけど、その、乱闘してたやつら」
lines.english: “They still haven’t caught the culprits, right? Though I don’t know if culprits is the right word. The people who were fighting, I mean.”

lines.japanese: 「みたい」
lines.english: “Apparently not.”

lines.japanese: 視点は固定したまま、小鳩がこっくり頷く。
lines.english: Without shifting her gaze, Kobato gave a small nod.

lines.japanese: 「意外と身近なところにいたりしてね」
lines.english: “Imagine if they turned out to be closer than we thought.”

lines.japanese: 「まさか」
lines.english: “Surely not.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は目を伏せるように食事を再開した。もしかしたら恐がらせてしまったのかもしれない。つくづく僕には冗談の才能がないみたいだ。
lines.english: She lowered her eyes and resumed eating. Perhaps I had frightened her. It seemed I truly had no gift for jokes.

lines.japanese: でも、いいや、とりあえず今日のノルマは果たした。明日からはパン以外の話もたくさんしよう。
lines.english: Still, never mind. I had met today's quota. Starting tomorrow, I would talk about plenty of things besides bread.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そういえば」
lines.english: “Oh, come to think of it.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「消しゴムが出来る前はパンを字消しに使ってて、それと区別する意味で食パンって呼ばれるようになったって説もあるらしいよ」
lines.english: “There’s also this theory that before erasers, people used bread to rub out writing, so they started calling the kind you ate ‘food bread’ to tell the two apart.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「でもこの説は年代的に無理があって、信憑性がかなり薄いらしいけど」
lines.english: “Though apparently the dates don’t really work, so that theory probably isn’t very reliable.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「そかー」
lines.english: “I seeee.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はちらちら僕に視線をよこしながら、緩慢に食事を進める。
lines.english: Kobato ate at a languid pace, stealing glances at me all the while.

lines.japanese: 僕は間欠的に甦る食パン豆ちしきをその都度語って聞かせ、なんとか息苦しい朝餉のときを凌いだ。
lines.english: Whenever another scrap of white-bread trivia returned to me, I shared it with her. Somehow, that carried me through the suffocating breakfast.
